The gate start-up chain end to end: eleven goals, in the order they unlock.

Your first hour

Written for the Async Industries start. The others reach the same place with less in hand.

Open the Operations tab — first on the bottom bar, bound to \ by default.

1. Restore power

The gate needs a real supply and a real reserve.

Ordinary generators and batteries. Nothing special is required, and nothing special is provided.

2. Build the gate

On Operations → Machine, designate four things:

A doorThis becomes the gate
A comms consoleThe controls
A batteryThe reserve
A machining tableWhere it gets assembled

Then run the assemble gate bill on the table:

100 steel + 8 industrial components

The table keeps all of its normal recipes.

3. Calibrate

A qualified staff member calibrates the gate once the assembly is done. The Machine pane numbers every step and shows which are complete.

4. Keep an operator on station

Someone stays at the console while a connection is open. This is a job, not a checkbox — walk them away and the connection drops.

5. Pick a crew

Up to three field staff. The planner checks skill, health and carried weight, and names anyone who is not ready.

It also shows who has been through before, and who has walked the exact address you are dialling. An operator who knows the route brings the gate up faster.

6. Open a connection and go

Bringing a connection up is work over time, not an instant. Walk away and it loses charge.

Read the refusal

Operations refuses any opening it cannot complete, and always names the reason:

  • the assembly is unfinished
  • the reserve is below what a return costs
  • no qualified operator is at the controls
  • no crew is ready
  • no validated way home
  • the gate is out of calibration
  • the connection was cut deliberately

The reason is the instruction. Fix the named one.

Then

  1. In the field, record a route, a distortion and an entity observation.
  2. Come home before the window closes.
  3. Analyse the recording at a bound laboratory. Analysis is pawn work over time.
  4. Have a second person review the finished report.
  5. Spend the insight on a company project.

That loop is the game.

Rimrooms — Async Industries. A development build; nothing here is a balance, performance or compatibility report.
